A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CONGO work. Their readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-G support reliable comparison, including the expanded Appendix F in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original quadratic-optimization experiments, Jackson-network simulations, DeathStarBench deployment measurements and supplementary runtime and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds sparsity-robustness and fixed-sampling-budget experiments in Appendix F.2-F.3.

M1.justification: The CONGO-B/Z/E procedures, recovery methods and gradient updates are retained; Algorithms 1 and 2 are unchanged. Appendix F.2 discusses adaptive sampling as future work, without incorporating it into the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: The quadratic-optimization, Jackson-network and SocialNetwork tasks remain. Appendix F.2 adds a controlled approximately sparse quadratic scenario with small nonzero background components, extending the synthetic input conditions beyond exactly sparse gradients.

E2.justification: No comparator is added or removed from corresponding existing experiments. The added studies reuse GD, GDSP and CONGO variants; NSGD, SGDSP and PPO retain their original comparison roles. The newly discussed Lasso approach is not evaluated.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce sparsity sweeps, deliberately incorrect supplied sparsity, excess cumulative cost relative to GD, and a fixed m=24 while dimension increases to 5000. Figure 9 gives GDSP a fixed 57-sample budget. These are additions within the existing quadratic simulation framework; retained benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained measurement-count sensitivity and gradient-limit analysis, Appendix F.2-F.3 adds systematic tests of weaker sparsity, approximate sparsity, sparsity misspecification and dimensional scaling under a fixed sampling budget. These substantially expand scrutiny of the method's central assumptions and practical robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions state 50 numerical-experiment seeds, identified as 0-49, with standard-deviation shading, five Jackson-network seeds and four deployment runs. No changed repetition counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Figures 8-10 add substantive findings: CONGO-Z/E remain close to GD across increased sparsity counts, retain advantages with approximately sparse gradients, and tolerate moderate sparsity misspecification but deteriorate under severe underestimation. CONGO-E also tracks GD through d=5000 with m=24. Existing result figures and their reported findings are retained.

T1.justification: Assumption 2 explicitly quantifies sparsity over all x in K. Appendix F.2 adds limited mathematical reasoning about a normalized measurement-residual proxy and finite-difference bias in prospective adaptive sampling. The principal theorems and Appendix C proofs remain unchanged apart from notation and reference edits.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the sparse zeroth-order OCO framework, three variants, dimension-independent O(sqrt(T)) regret, sampling-efficiency claims and practical autoscaling benefits. The new experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2 explains CONGO-B's deterioration under overestimated sparsity through increased measurement interference and discusses the runtime cost of excessive sampling and possible adaptive selection. Appendix F.3 explicitly limits its dimensional-scaling interpretation to fixed sparsity. These add practical qualifications to the retained limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct CONGO code-repository pointer on the first page, supplementing the existing references to supplementary code and upstream ZORO code. Appendix F.2-F.3 specifies the new objective construction and sampling settings; existing implementation descriptions, hardware information and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Appendix A adds a substantive discussion of Wang et al. (2018), distinguishing its static Lasso-based gradient estimation and stated quadratic sparsity dependence from CONGO. Appendix F.2 also discusses adapting Cai et al. (2022)'s sampling strategy to OCO.

P1.justification: v3 consolidates repetitive related-work prose, makes localized wording and notation edits, adds an explanatory remark and two Appendix F subsections, and updates author information and acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 8-10, renumbers the retained network and workflow diagrams as Figures 11-12, and adjusts float placement and title/header formatting. Existing figure artwork and table structures are retained, so the visual revision is localized rather than a redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's measurement-count analysis and application evidence, v3 supplies useful controlled tests of approximate and unknown sparsity and fixed-budget scaling, exposing both strengths and failure conditions. Clearer research positioning and code-access information also help. These strengthen practical confidence within the existing synthetic framework, while the main guarantees and application evidence remain unchanged.
